Definition: from G5384 and G80; fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal:--love as brethren.
BiblicalUsage: Philadelphos means loving as brethren, fraternal, and it appears once, in Peter's call to unity. He tells the brethren to be all of one mind, having compassion one of another, and to love as brethren, to be pitiful and courteous.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that loving as brethren is the church's family rule: one mind, one compassion, and a love that treats every believer as blood kin.
